newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Fire blight bacteria discovered in Australia - govt.
newsitem.headline: Fire blight bacteria discovered in Australia - govt.

text.p: Australian Primary Industries Minister John Anderson said on Wednesday fire blight bacteria, a major apple and pear pest, had been found in Australia for the first time.
Export markets had been told of the outbreak, discovered in plants in Victoria state, but it was not expected to affect access for Australian fruit, he said in a statement.
The bacteria was found on cotoneaster and other shrubs in the botanical gardens in the Victorian capital, Melbourne, and more searches are underway.
Anderson said the outbreak would not affect Canberra's plan to reject New Zealand apple imports.
Australia's quarantine service said last month it would reject New Zealand apples because they could carry fire blight.
State and territory officials and industry representatives would meet in Melbourne on Thursday to discuss the outbreak.
Local media reports say the blight was first spotted in the botanical gardens by a visiting New Zealand scientist who took some clippings home with him to test.
